prompt: On a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 VM, investigate one boot-to-service-readiness path for a service other than systemd-journald.service. Choose an approved localhost readiness operation that is read-only, requires no credential, and causes no business side effect; never contact an employer or production endpoint. Produce a boot-ID-scoped explanation that distinguishes kernel time, userspace ordering, unit state, journal evidence, and the readiness result. Do not change the boot loader, kernel command line, system units, or journal retention.
deliverables: A sanitized environment card naming Ubuntu version, virtualization context, PID 1, kernel release, boot ID, privilege used, and why the VM is disposable.
A diagram showing firmware or VM start, kernel and initramfs, root filesystem, systemd target or dependencies, chosen service, and the readiness boundary.
A timestamped evidence table with each command, relevant output, what it proves, what it does not prove, and the next hypothesis.
A short incident narrative naming the first observed divergence, at least two rejected hypotheses, the safest recovery decision, and one prevention improvement.

A cleanup-boundary statement listing the documented read-only commands, confirming that the task defined no lesson-owned persistent resource or long-running process, and acknowledging that ordinary command processes and access or audit records may exist.
evidenceRequirements: Use the same boot ID across the correlated kernel, systemd, journal, and readiness evidence.
Include systemd-analyze time plus either critical-chain or an explicitly justified equivalent when PID 1 is systemd.
Include structured unit properties rather than relying only on the human-oriented systemctl status summary.
Use a bounded journal query with a stated boot, unit or kernel scope, time window or line limit, and no pager.
Use a service other than systemd-journald.service and demonstrate the difference between active state and a credential-free, side-effect-free localhost readiness operation.
Redact hostnames, usernames, addresses, tokens, employer data, and any production identifiers before review.

rubric.observableEvidence: Uses a disposable VM, states privilege and abort conditions, remains read-only, and submits a bounded cleanup statement without relying on shell history or claiming that observation leaves no records.
Explains ownership and handoffs from kernel through PID 1, dependencies, service state, and readiness without collapsing the layers.
Every important command is tied to a question, proof boundary, observed branch, and safe next evidence.
Identifies a first divergence, rejects plausible alternatives with evidence, and reaches a bounded recovery decision without a supplied answer path.
Connects the VM investigation to a measurable readiness SLI, prevention control, and rollback-aware operating practice.
